requirements: conf must be initialized.
allow_legacy must be one of MBEDTLS_SSL_LEGACY_NO_RENEGOTIATION, MBEDTLS_SSL_LEGACY_ALLOW_RENEGOTIATION, MBEDTLS_SSL_LEGACY_BREAK_HANDSHAKE.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_conf_renegotiation_enforced
functions.description: Control whether to enforce our renegotiation requests and for how many records to allow as a grace period before closing if the peer ignores the request.
requirements: conf must be initialized.
max_records = MBEDTLS_SSL_RENEGOTIATION_NOT_ENFORCED disables enforcement; non-negative values enable enforcement with grace period.
Client-side grace period only applies during mbedtls_ssl_read().

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_conf_renegotiation_period
functions.description: Set record-counter threshold for periodic renegotiation (big-endian 64-bit). Prevents counter wrap and enables policy-based key refresh.
requirements: conf must be initialized.
period points to 8 bytes big-endian threshold.
Max period depends on transport: DTLS up to 2^48-1, TLS up to 2^64-1.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_check_pending
functions.description: Return 1 if there is unprocessed data in the SSL layer (any type), 0 otherwise. Useful to decide whether to wait on the transport or process internal data.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pointer.
A return of 1 does not guarantee that mbedtls_ssl_read() will return application data; internal messages may be pending.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_bytes_avail
functions.description: Return number of unread application data bytes remaining in the current record’s buffer.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Useful with datagram transport to detect datagram boundaries.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_verify_result
functions.description: Return the X.509 verification result flags for the peer certificate: 0 on success, -1u if not available, or a bitmask of MBEDTLS_X509_BADCERT_XXX/MBEDTLS_X509_BADCRL_XXX.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Call after (attempted) handshake. -1u indicates result not available (e.g., handshake aborted early).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_ciphersuite_id_from_ssl
functions.description: Return the ciphersuite ID negotiated for the current connection.
requirements: ssl must be valid and handshake completed.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_ciphersuite
functions.description: Return the name of the currently negotiated ciphersuite.
requirements: ssl must be valid and handshake completed.
Returned string is library-owned; do not free or modify.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_version
functions.description: Return a string representation of the negotiated TLS version.
requirements: ssl must be valid and handshake progressed sufficiently.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_record_expansion
functions.description: Return maximum number of bytes added by record layer (header + AEAD/MAC overhead, padding) for current connection.
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_max_out_record_payload
functions.description: Return current maximum payload size allowed for an outgoing record given configuration, negotiated extensions, DTLS MTU, and record expansion.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
With DTLS, mbedtls_ssl_write() will error if asked to send more than this; with TLS it will fragment.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_max_in_record_payload
functions.description: Return current maximum payload size expected for an incoming record given configuration, negotiated extensions, and record expansion.
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_peer_cert
functions.description: Return a pointer to the current peer certificate, if available. The pointer is owned by the SSL context and may become invalid after any SSL API call.
requirements: ssl must be valid and constructed with X.509 enabled.
Do not use the returned pointer after any further SSL API call unless you copy it. May return NULL if no peer cert is available or memory saving option freed it.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_session
functions.description: Client: export a session for later resumption (TLS 1.2 ID or ticket; TLS 1.3 tickets if enabled).
requirements: ssl must be a valid context with a completed handshake.
session must be initialized with mbedtls_ssl_session_init() and unused.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_handshake
functions.description: Run or resume the SSL/TLS handshake on a connection until completion or until the operation would block/asynchronous operation in progress. May need to be called repeatedly.
requirements: ssl must be initialized, set up with mbedtls_ssl_setup(), I/O callbacks set (mbedtls_ssl_set_bio()), and for DTLS timers set (mbedtls_ssl_set_timer_cb()).

Caller must handle non-fatal returns: MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ/WRITE, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_ASYNC_IN_PROGRESS, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_CRYPTO_IN_PROGRESS, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_HELLO_VERIFY_REQUIRED (DTLS), MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_RECEIVED_EARLY_DATA (server with early data enabled).
On any other error, the context must not be used for I/O until reset or freed.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_handshake_step
functions.description: Advance the handshake state machine by a single step. Use with mbedtls_ssl_is_handshake_over() to control progression.
requirements: ssl must be initialized and handshake started.
Do not call after handshake is over (check mbedtls_ssl_is_handshake_over()).
Same return/error handling requirements as mbedtls_ssl_handshake().

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_renegotiate
functions.description: Initiate renegotiation on an established connection. Client performs immediately; server requests and will proceed during next read if peer honors.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, connected context with renegotiation support configured as needed.
Same non-fatal returns as handshake; on other errors, reset or free the context before reuse.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_read
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_read(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Read up to len bytes of application data. Handles handshake progression as needed. May return non-fatal WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE/ASYNC/CRYPTO_IN_PROGRESS/CLIENT_RECONNECT/RECEIVED_EARLY_DATA.
requirements: ssl must be initialized, set up, and have I/O callbacks set.
buf must point to writable memory of at least len bytes.
Caller must handle 0 (EOF without close_notify) and MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_PEER_CLOSE_NOTIFY appropriately by closing/resetting the connection.
On other fatal errors, stop using the context until reset or free.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_write
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_write(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Write up to len bytes of application data. May perform partial writes; must be called again with remaining data until complete. Handles handshake progression as needed.
requirements: ssl must be initialized and set up with I/O callbacks.
buf must point to readable memory of at least len bytes.
Caller must handle partial writes and non-fatal returns WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE/ASYNC/CRYPTO_IN_PROGRESS/RECEIVED_EARLY_DATA by retrying with same arguments when appropriate.
If len exceeds max out record payload: TLS fragments; DTLS returns PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_send_alert_message
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_send_alert_message(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, unsigned char level, unsigned char message);
functions.description: Send a TLS alert with given level and description.
requirements: ssl must be valid and set up with I/O callbacks.
level must be MBEDTLS_SSL_ALERT_LEVEL_WARNING or MBEDTLS_SSL_ALERT_LEVEL_FATAL; message should be one of MBEDTLS_SSL_ALERT_MSG_*.
On return other than 0 or WANT_READ/WRITE, the connection must be closed or reset before reuse.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_close_notify
functions.description: Send a close_notify alert to the peer indicating the connection is being closed gracefully.
requirements: ssl must be valid and set up with I/O callbacks.
On return other than 0 or WANT_READ/WRITE, the context must be closed/reset before reuse.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_read_early_data
functions.description: Server: read up to len bytes of TLS 1.3 early data when previous API returned MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_RECEIVED_EARLY_DATA.
requirements: ssl must be a server-side context with early data enabled by configuration.
Call only after mbedtls_ssl_handshake()/handshake_step()/read()/write() returned MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_RECEIVED_EARLY_DATA.
buf must point to writable memory of size len.
Returns PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT on invalid input or MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_CANNOT_READ_EARLY_DATA if early data cannot be read for this context.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_write_early_data
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_write_early_data(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Client: write up to len bytes of early application data (0-RTT) during handshake when configured with an eligible PSK.
requirements: ssl must be a client context configured for early data with a PSK that allows early data.
buf must point to readable memory of size len.
May start the handshake; does not indicate whether server accepted early data.
Returns MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_CANNOT_WRITE_EARLY_DATA if early data is not/ no longer possible for this context.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_early_data_status
functions.description: Client: after handshake completion, query whether early data was indicated and whether the server accepted or rejected it.
requirements: ssl must be a client context and the handshake must be completed; otherwise returns PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_free
functions.description: Free resources referenced by an SSL context and clear its memory.
requirements: ssl may be NULL or previously initialized; safe to call on a zeroed or initialized context.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_context_save
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_context_save(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, unsigned char *buf, size_t buf_len, size_t *olen);
functions.description: Serialize an active DTLS 1.2 AEAD connection’s resumable state into a buffer and reset the SSL context for reuse, enabling transparent later restoration.
requirements: ssl must represent an active connection with no handshake in progress and no pending I/O.
Only supported for DTLS 1.2 with an AEAD ciphersuite and with renegotiation disabled; otherwise returns PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.
buf may be NULL with buf_len=0 to query required size in olen.
On success, the context is reset and detached from the saved connection.
Caller must handle PSA_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and PSA_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_context_load
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_context_load(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Load previously serialized connection state into a prepared SSL context to resume an active connection transparently.
requirements: ssl must be prepared: initialized, set up with the same mbedtls_ssl_config as the original connection (via mbedtls_ssl_setup()), or reset via mbedtls_ssl_session_reset() on such context; no handshake must have been performed between setup/reset and this call.
After loading, reconfigure per-connection callbacks (mbedtls_ssl_set_bio, mbedtls_ssl_set_timer_cb, user data) as needed, since they are not restored.
On error, this function calls mbedtls_ssl_free(ssl); the caller must reinitialize if needed.
buf must point to the serialized data obtained from mbedtls_ssl_context_save().

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_config_init
functions.description: Initialize an SSL configuration to a clean state ready for defaults or manual configuration.
requirements: conf must be a valid pointer to writable memory.
Call mbedtls_ssl_config_defaults() unless configuring all fields manually.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_config_defaults
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_config_defaults(mbedtls_ssl_config *conf, int endpoint, int transport, int preset);
functions.description: Load reasonable default configuration values for a client/server, TLS/DTLS, and preset profile.
requirements: conf must be initialized with mbedtls_ssl_config_init().
endpoint must be MBEDTLS_SSL_IS_CLIENT or MBEDTLS_SSL_IS_SERVER.
transport must be MBEDTLS_SSL_TRANSPORT_STREAM or MBEDTLS_SSL_TRANSPORT_DATAGRAM.
preset must be a MBEDTLS_SSL_PRESET_* value.
Returns 0 or allocation failure error (MBEDTLS_ERR_XXX_ALLOC_FAILED per header note).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_config_free
functions.description: Free resources referenced by an SSL configuration and clear its memory.
requirements: conf may be NULL or previously initialized; safe to call on zeroed or initialized object.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_session_init
functions.description: Initialize an SSL session object to a clean state for later population, save, or load.
requirements: session must be a valid pointer to writable memory.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_session_free
functions.description: Free resources referenced by an SSL session (including peer cert if kept) and clear its memory.
requirements: session may be NULL or previously initialized; safe to call.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_tls_prf
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_tls_prf(const mbedtls_tls_prf_types prf, const unsigned char *secret, size_t slen, const char *label, const unsigned char *random, size_t rlen, unsigned char *dstbuf, size_t dlen);
functions.description: Compute TLS PRF/HKDF expand depending on selected prf type, deriving key material from secret, label and random bytes into dstbuf.
requirements: prf must be one of mbedtls_tls_prf_types values supported by the build.
secret/label/random must point to valid buffers of lengths slen/strlen(label)+1 (NUL-terminated)/rlen respectively.
dstbuf must have at least dlen bytes.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an SSL-specific error.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_export_keying_material
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_export_keying_material(mbedtls_ssl_context *ssl, uint8_t *out, const size_t key_len, const char *label, const size_t label_len, const unsigned char *context, const size_t context_len, const int use_context);
functions.description: Export application keying material from an established session (TLS exporter) into out buffer using the provided label and optional context.
requirements: ssl must have completed the handshake; otherwise returns PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.
out must have at least key_len bytes; key_len must be <= MBEDTLS_SSL_EXPORT_MAX_KEY_LEN (8160).
label_len must be at most 249 in TLS 1.3.
If use_context is 0, TLS 1.3 uses empty context and ignores context/context_len; TLS 1.2 distinguishes between no context and empty context.
context/context_len must obey TLS limits (context_len < 2^16 in TLS 1.2).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_set_export_keys_cb
functions.description: Attach a key export callback to an SSL context to observe/export key material and randoms during handshakes (e.g., for NSS key log or custom exporters).
requirements: ssl must be initialized.
f_export_keys may be NULL to clear; when set, it will be called with pointers valid at callback time; callback must not block excessively.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_conf_async_private_cb
functions.description: Configure callbacks to offload private key operations asynchronously (start, resume, cancel) and attach opaque configuration data.
requirements: conf must be initialized.
If f_async_sign is NULL, f_async_resume may be NULL; otherwise f_async_resume must be non-NULL.
config_data is stored without dereferencing; must remain valid as needed.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_conf_get_async_config_data
functions.description: Retrieve the configuration data pointer previously set for async private operations.
requirements: conf must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_get_async_operation_data
functions.description: During a handshake, retrieve the per-operation user context last set for an asynchronous private operation.
requirements: ssl must be valid and a handshake must be in progress; otherwise behavior is returning NULL per docs.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_set_async_operation_data
functions.description: During a handshake, set the per-operation user context associated with an ongoing asynchronous private key operation.
requirements: ssl must be valid and a handshake must be in progress.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_init
functions.description: Initialize an SSL session cache context. Sets up the cache structure to be ready for use by the cache get/set/remove APIs. Typically called once on a freshly allocated context before any other cache operations.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_ssl_cache_context.
Call this before using the context with mbedtls_ssl_cache_get, mbedtls_ssl_cache_set, mbedtls_ssl_cache_remove, or other cache APIs (inferred from typical init pattern).
Thread-safety: the function itself has no special notes; subsequent cache operations are thread-safe only if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled (module note).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_get
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_cache_get(void *data, unsigned char const *session_id, size_t session_id_len, mbedtls_ssl_session *session);
functions.description: Lookup a serialized SSL session by its session ID in the cache and load it into the provided session object. Intended for use as the SSL session cache get callback. Thread-safe if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled.
requirements: data must point to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred from parameter documentation: "The SSL cache context to use.").
session_id must point to a buffer of at least session_id_len bytes holding the session ID.
session_id_len is the length in bytes of session_id; it must match the actual size of the provided buffer.
session must be a valid, writable mbedtls_ssl_session pointer to receive the loaded session if found.

Return handling: returns 0 on success; returns MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_CACHE_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND if no entry with the specified session ID exists; other negative error codes indicate failures. Callers must check and handle nonzero returns.
Thread-safety: safe to call concurrently only if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_set
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_cache_set(void *data, unsigned char const *session_id, size_t session_id_len, const mbedtls_ssl_session *session);
functions.description: Store an SSL session in the cache under the given session ID. Intended for use as the SSL session cache set callback. Thread-safe if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled.
requirements: data must point to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred from parameter documentation).
session_id must point to a buffer of at least session_id_len bytes holding the session ID associated with session.
session_id_len is the length in bytes of session_id; it must match the actual size of the provided buffer.
session must point to a valid mbedtls_ssl_session to be stored.
Return handling: returns 0 on success; negative error code on failure. Callers must check for and handle negative returns.
Thread-safety: safe to call concurrently only if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_remove
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_cache_remove(void *data, unsigned char const *session_id, size_t session_id_len);
functions.description: Remove the cache entry identified by the given session ID. If the entry does not exist, success (0) is still returned. Thread-safe if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled.
requirements: data must point to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred from parameter documentation).
session_id must point to a buffer of at least session_id_len bytes holding the session ID to remove.
session_id_len is the length in bytes of session_id; it must match the actual size of the provided buffer.
Return handling: returns 0 on success (including when the entry does not exist); negative error code on failure. Callers must check and handle negative returns.
Thread-safety: safe to call concurrently only if MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is enabled.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_set_timeout
functions.description: Set the cache entry timeout (in seconds). A timeout of 0 disables expiration. Default is MBEDTLS_SSL_CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (1 day). Available only when MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME is enabled.
requirements: This function is available only if MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME is enabled at compile time.
cache must be a valid pointer to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred).
timeout is in seconds; a value of 0 means no timeout. Other range constraints are not specified.
Callers should ensure subsequent cache operations respect the configured timeout semantics (inferred from purpose).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_get_timeout
functions.description: Get the current cache entry timeout (in seconds). Returns 0 if timeouts are disabled. Available only when MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME is enabled.
requirements: This function is available only if MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME is enabled at compile time.
cache must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_set_max_entries
functions.description: Set the maximum number of entries to keep in the cache. Default is MBEDTLS_SSL_CACHE_DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES (50).
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred).
max specifies the maximum number of cache entries; no explicit range constraints are documented.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cache_free
functions.description: Free referenced items in an SSL cache context and clear memory. Call when the cache is no longer needed to release resources.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_ssl_cache_context (inferred).
Should be called after prior initialization with mbedtls_ssl_cache_init (inferred from typical lifecycle).
After calling, the context must not be used unless re-initialized (inferred).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_init
functions.description: Initialize a DTLS cookie context. Sets the context to a valid, default-initialized state so it can be used with subsequent cookie operations (setup, write/check via the default callbacks, free). Typical usage: allocate a mbedtls_ssl_cookie_ctx, call this initializer, then call mbedtls_ssl_cookie_setup before using the context to create/verify cookies.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to mbedtls_ssl_cookie_ctx.
Must be called before using the context with other cookie-related functions such as mbedtls_ssl_cookie_setup, mbedtls_ssl_cookie_set_timeout, or mbedtls_ssl_cookie_free.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_setup
functions.description: Prepare a DTLS cookie context for use by generating/setting up the cryptographic material (keys/algorithm) needed for HMAC-based cookie generation and verification. Typical usage: call after mbedtls_ssl_cookie_init and optionally before registering the cookie callbacks with the SSL configuration.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cookie_ctx (initialize with mbedtls_ssl_cookie_init first).
Caller must check the returned int status; by Mbed TLS convention, 0 indicates success and a negative error code indicates failure (exact codes not specified here).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_set_timeout
functions.description: Set the expiration policy for generated DTLS cookies for the given context. The delay is expressed in seconds if MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME is enabled, or as a count of cookies issued otherwise. A delay of 0 disables expiration (not recommended). Call after initialization (and optionally setup) to override the default MBEDTLS_SSL_COOKIE_TIMEOUT.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized mbedtls_ssl_cookie_ctx.
delay is interpreted as seconds if MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME is defined, or as number of cookies issued otherwise.
Setting delay to 0 disables expiration (explicitly allowed but noted as NOT recommended in the documentation).

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_free
functions.description: Release resources held by a DTLS cookie context. After this call, the context is no longer usable until reinitialized with mbedtls_ssl_cookie_init. Safe to call when cleaning up after handshake operations.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer (non-NULL) to a mbedtls_ssl_cookie_ctx; the context should have been initialized before.
After calling, the context must be reinitialized with mbedtls_ssl_cookie_init before reuse.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_write
functions.signature: unknown (declared as: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_write_t mbedtls_ssl_cookie_write; exact function pointer signature not present in this header)
functions.description: Default DTLS cookie generation callback implementation. Exposed as a function pointer variable matching the typedef mbedtls_ssl_cookie_write_t; intended to be used where a DTLS cookie write/generation callback is required. Exact parameters and return type are defined by the typedef, which is not included in this header.
requirements: unknown (the parameter and return types, and any preconditions, are defined by mbedtls_ssl_cookie_write_t and are not present in this header)

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_check
functions.signature: unknown (declared as: mbedtls_ssl_cookie_check_t mbedtls_ssl_cookie_check; exact function pointer signature not present in this header)
functions.description: Default DTLS cookie verification callback implementation. Exposed as a function pointer variable matching the typedef mbedtls_ssl_cookie_check_t; intended to be used where a DTLS cookie verification/check callback is required. Exact parameters and return type are defined by the typedef, which is not included in this header.
requirements: unknown (the parameter and return types, and any preconditions, are defined by mbedtls_ssl_cookie_check_t and are not present in this header)

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_ticket_init
functions.description: Initialize an mbedtls_ssl_ticket_context so it can be passed to mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup() or mbedtls_ssl_ticket_free(). Does not allocate external resources beyond preparing the context fields.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer.
Call this before mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup() or mbedtls_ssl_ticket_free().
No return value; there is no error reporting from this function.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup(mbedtls_ssl_ticket_context *ctx, psa_algorithm_t alg, psa_key_type_t key_type, psa_key_bits_t key_bits, uint32_t lifetime);
functions.description: Prepare the ticket context for use by configuring the AEAD algorithm and PSA key parameters used to protect TLS session tickets, and by establishing ticket lifetime. Typically called once after mbedtls_ssl_ticket_init() and before attaching the callbacks to an SSL configuration.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with mbedtls_ssl_ticket_init().
alg must identify an AEAD algorithm suitable for ticket protection.
key_type must be a PSA cryptographic key type compatible with alg.
key_bits must be a valid size for key_type/alg (e.g., matches algorithm requirements).
lifetime is in seconds; recommended value is 86400 (one day).
If TLS 1.3 session tickets are sent after the handshake, lifetime must be less than seven days; otherwise the connection will fail when attempting to send the first ticket.
On success returns 0; on failure returns a specific MBEDTLS_ERR_XXX error code which the caller must check and handle.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_ticket_rotate
functions.signature: int mbedtls_ssl_ticket_rotate(mbedtls_ssl_ticket_context *ctx, const unsigned char *name, size_t nlength, const unsigned char *k, size_t klength, uint32_t lifetime);
functions.description: Rotate the session ticket encryption key to the externally supplied key and key name. This allows coordinated rotation across machines; if not used, the module rotates keys internally when needed to avoid unbounded key lifetimes.
requirements: ctx must have been set up via mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup().
name must point to the session ticket key name data; recommended to be cryptographically random.
nlength must equal sizeof(ctx->keys[ctx->active].name), i.e., MBEDTLS_SSL_TICKET_KEY_NAME_BYTES (4 bytes).
k must point to the new session ticket encryption key material; recommended to be cryptographically random.
klength must be sufficient for the cipher specified in mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup() (i.e., appropriate for the configured alg/key_type/key_bits).
lifetime is in seconds; recommended value is 86400 (one day).
If TLS 1.3 session tickets are sent after the handshake, lifetime must be less than seven days; otherwise the connection will fail when attempting to send the first ticket.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise returns a specific MBEDTLS_ERR_XXX error code which the caller must check and handle.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_ticket_write
functions.description: Implementation instance of the ticket write callback (type mbedtls_ssl_ticket_write_t). It is intended to be assigned as the ticket write callback in an SSL configuration and invoked by the SSL stack to produce a session ticket. The exact function pointer signature is defined by the typedef mbedtls_ssl_ticket_write_t (not present in this header excerpt).
requirements: Signature and argument requirements are defined by the typedef mbedtls_ssl_ticket_write_t in the library headers (refer to its documentation).
Requires that the associated mbedtls_ssl_ticket_context has been set up (typically via mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup()).
Caller must follow the return/error-handling contract specified by mbedtls_ssl_ticket_write_t.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_ticket_parse
functions.description: Implementation instance of the ticket parse callback (type mbedtls_ssl_ticket_parse_t). It is intended to be assigned as the ticket parse callback in an SSL configuration and invoked by the SSL stack to decrypt/validate a received session ticket. The exact function pointer signature is defined by the typedef mbedtls_ssl_ticket_parse_t (not present in this header excerpt).
requirements: Signature and argument requirements are defined by the typedef mbedtls_ssl_ticket_parse_t in the library headers (refer to its documentation).
Requires that the associated mbedtls_ssl_ticket_context has been set up (typically via mbedtls_ssl_ticket_setup()).
Caller must follow the return/error-handling contract specified by mbedtls_ssl_ticket_parse_t.

functions.name: mbedtls_ssl_ticket_free
functions.description: Free and zeroize the contents of an mbedtls_ssl_ticket_context, releasing any resources acquired during setup or rotation. Safe to call after mbedtls_ssl_ticket_init() and after failed or successful setup.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer (may be uninitialized only if it has just been zeroed/initialized by mbedtls_ssl_ticket_init()).
After calling, the context contents are zeroized; the context must be reinitialized with mbedtls_ssl_ticket_init() before reuse.
No return value; there is no error reporting from this function.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_init
functions.description: Initialize an mbedtls_net_context so it is safe to use with other net_* functions or to free later. Typical first call before connect/bind/accept.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to mbedtls_net_context.
Call this before using ctx in other mbedtls_net_* operations or before freeing it.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_connect
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_connect(mbedtls_net_context *ctx, const char *host, const char *port, int proto);
functions.description: Create and connect a socket in ctx to host:port using the specified protocol (TCP or UDP). For UDP, the socket is put into a connected mode to fix a peer. Returns 0 on success or a negative MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_* code on failure.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via mbedtls_net_init and not already connected.
host must be a valid, null-terminated hostname or IP address string resolvable on the system.
port must be a valid, null-terminated service/port string (e.g., "443").
proto must be MBEDTLS_NET_PROTO_TCP or MBEDTLS_NET_PROTO_UDP.
Caller must handle error returns: MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_SOCKET_FAILED, MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_UNKNOWN_HOST, MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_CONNECT_FAILED.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_bind
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_bind(mbedtls_net_context *ctx, const char *bind_ip, const char *port, int proto);
functions.description: Create a socket and bind it to bind_ip:port for the chosen protocol. For TCP, the socket is put into listening state. For UDP, the socket is just opened and bound.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via mbedtls_net_init and not already in use.
bind_ip may be NULL to bind on all interfaces; otherwise must be a valid, null-terminated local IP/address string.
port must be a valid, null-terminated service/port string (e.g., "443").
proto must be MBEDTLS_NET_PROTO_TCP or MBEDTLS_NET_PROTO_UDP.
Caller must handle possible errors: MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_SOCKET_FAILED, MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_UNKNOWN_HOST, MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_BIND_FAILED, MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_LISTEN_FAILED.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_accept
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_accept(mbedtls_net_context *bind_ctx, mbedtls_net_context *client_ctx, void *client_ip, size_t buf_size, size_t *cip_len);
functions.description: Accept a new TCP connection on bind_ctx, placing the resulting connected socket into client_ctx. Optionally returns the peer IP address into client_ip. Non-blocking sockets may return MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ if accept would block.
requirements: bind_ctx must refer to a valid, bound and listening TCP socket created by mbedtls_net_bind with TCP.
client_ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to mbedtls_net_context to receive the accepted socket (it should be initialized or at least valid for assignment).
client_ip may be NULL; if not NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of size buf_size to receive the textual or binary IP representation as implemented by the platform.
If client_ip is not NULL, buf_size must be large enough; otherwise PSA_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL is returned and cip_len is set per implementation.
cip_len may be NULL only if client_ip is NULL; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to receive the number of bytes written to client_ip.
If bind_ctx is non-blocking and no connection is pending, caller must handle MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_poll
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_poll(mbedtls_net_context *ctx, uint32_t rw, uint32_t timeout);
functions.description: Wait until ctx is ready for reading and/or writing as specified by rw bitmask. Returns a bitmask of MBEDTLS_NET_POLL_READ/WRITE on success or timeout, or a negative error code on failure. Uses select(); very large file descriptors (>= FD_SETSIZE) cause an error.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid socket (typically obtained via connect, bind/accept).
rw must be a bitwise OR of MBEDTLS_NET_POLL_READ and/or MBEDTLS_NET_POLL_WRITE; at least one should be set.
timeout is in milliseconds: 0 returns immediately; 0xFFFFFFFF (i.e., (uint32_t)-1) blocks potentially indefinitely.
Caller must handle negative error returns and interpret the returned bitmask.
On platforms where select() cannot handle fd >= FD_SETSIZE, caller should avoid such descriptors or handle failure.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_set_block
functions.description: Set the underlying socket in ctx to blocking mode.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid, open socket.
Caller must handle a non-zero (error) return code.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_set_nonblock
functions.description: Set the underlying socket in ctx to non-blocking mode.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid, open socket.
Caller must handle a non-zero (error) return code.
Subsequent I/O may return MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ/WRITE and callers must handle these appropriately.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_usleep
functions.description: Sleep for approximately usec microseconds. Actual sleep resolution is limited by select()’s timeout granularity (typically ~10 ms).
requirements: usec is the number of microseconds to sleep; large values may be clamped by platform limits.
Callers should not assume sub-10ms precision due to platform granularity.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_recv
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_recv(void *ctx, unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Receive up to len bytes from the socket referenced by ctx, writing them into buf. Returns number of bytes received, or a negative error code. On non-blocking sockets, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ indicates the operation would block.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_net_context (as provided to Mbed TLS I/O callbacks) with an open socket.
buf must be a valid, writable buffer of at least len bytes when len > 0.
Caller must handle partial reads (return value may be < len), zero or positive counts, and negative MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_* or MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ returns.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_send
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_send(void *ctx, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Send up to len bytes from buf to the socket referenced by ctx. Returns number of bytes sent, or a negative error code. On non-blocking sockets, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_WRITE indicates the operation would block.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_net_context with an open socket.
buf must be a valid, readable buffer of at least len bytes when len > 0.
Caller must handle partial writes (return value may be < len) and negative MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_* or MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_WRITE returns.

functions.name: mbedtls_net_recv_timeout
functions.signature: int mbedtls_net_recv_timeout(void *ctx, unsigned char *buf, size_t len, uint32_t timeout);
functions.description: Receive up to len bytes with a maximum wait of timeout milliseconds. Returns the number of bytes received on success; MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_TIMEOUT on timeout; MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ if interrupted by a signal; or another negative MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_* code on other failures. Uses select(); fd >= FD_SETSIZE is an error. This call blocks until data or timeout even if the socket is non-blocking.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_net_context with an open socket.
buf must be a valid, writable buffer of at least len bytes when len > 0.
timeout is in milliseconds; 0 means wait indefinitely.
Caller must handle all documented negative return codes and partial reads.
Be aware of select() limitations with very large file descriptors (>= FD_SETSIZE).

functions.name: mbedtls_net_close
functions.description: Close the underlying connection and free/clear associated data in ctx. Does not free the ctx object itself.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer; after return, the context is no longer connected and must be re-initialized or reconnected before reuse.
Caller is responsible for the lifetime of the memory pointed to by ctx (this function does not free ctx).

functions.name: mbedtls_net_free
functions.description: Gracefully shut down the connection (if applicable) and free/clear associated data in ctx. Does not free the ctx object itself.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer; after return, the context is cleared and not usable until re-initialized.
Caller is responsible for the memory pointed to by ctx (this function does not free ctx).

functions.name: mbedtls_timing_get_timer
functions.signature: unsigned long mbedtls_timing_get_timer(struct mbedtls_timing_hr_time *val, int reset);
functions.description: Internal timing helper that operates on a high-resolution timer context. Typically used to start/reset a timer when reset is non-zero and to return the elapsed time (often in milliseconds) since the last reset when reset is zero. Marked for internal use; external callers should prefer the delay APIs unless they know the timing subsystem. Exact units and semantics may vary with the platform or alternative timing implementation (MBEDTLS_TIMING_ALT).
requirements: val must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid struct mbedtls_timing_hr_time instance.

reset usage is implementation-defined; commonly, reset != 0 initializes/resets the timer and returns 0, and reset == 0 returns the elapsed time since the last reset (inferred from typical Mbed TLS usage; exact behavior is not explicitly documented here).
Callers should not rely on this function if MBEDTLS_TIMING_ALT provides a different implementation; behavior is platform-dependent.
No explicit error reporting is defined; callers must treat the return value as a duration/measurement and not as a status code.

functions.name: mbedtls_timing_set_delay
functions.signature: void mbedtls_timing_set_delay(void *data, uint32_t int_ms, uint32_t fin_ms);
functions.description: Configure a pair of timeouts (intermediate and final) associated with a timing delay context, for use with mbedtls_timing_get_delay(). Passing fin_ms = 0 cancels the current delay. To set a single delay, either call the lower-level timer API directly or pass int_ms == fin_ms.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid mbedtls_timing_delay_context object.
int_ms is the intermediate delay in milliseconds.
fin_ms is the final delay in milliseconds; set to 0 to cancel.
The effect of int_ms > fin_ms is unspecified by the documentation and should be avoided.
The provided context must remain valid and unchanged (except by this API) between set and subsequent get calls.
No return value is provided; callers should use mbedtls_timing_get_delay() to observe state.

functions.name: mbedtls_timing_get_delay
functions.description: Query the status of the delays configured by mbedtls_timing_set_delay(), returning whether none, the intermediate, or the final delay has expired. Also returns -1 if the delay was cancelled (fin_ms = 0). Intended for polling in loops to implement timeouts.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid mbedtls_timing_delay_context previously used with mbedtls_timing_set_delay().

Return values: -1 if cancelled (fin_ms = 0), 0 if no delay has passed, 1 if only the intermediate delay has passed, 2 if the final delay has passed. Callers must handle all return codes appropriately.
The context must have been initialized/set via mbedtls_timing_set_delay() before calling; otherwise behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: mbedtls_timing_get_final_delay
functions.description: Return the configured final delay (in milliseconds) from the given timing delay context. This is a convenience accessor for code that needs to know the final timeout value.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid mbedtls_timing_delay_context.
The context should have been set by mbedtls_timing_set_delay() to return a meaningful value.
No error reporting is defined; the function returns a 32-bit millisecond value.

functions.name: mbedtls_debug_set_threshold
functions.description: Sets the global debug verbosity threshold for the library’s debug output. Messages with a debug level greater than the threshold are discarded (0=no debug, 1=error, 2=state change, 3=informational, 4=verbose). Typical usage is to call this once at program startup (or adjust at runtime) to control how much debug information is emitted by the library.
requirements: threshold must be an integer in the range 0..4 inclusive, corresponding to the documented debug levels.
Affects global debug output filtering for the library; callers should be aware this is a global setting (thread-safety or multi-context behavior is not documented here).

functions.name: mbedtls_strerror
functions.signature: void mbedtls_strerror(int errnum, char *buffer, size_t buflen);
functions.description: Translate an Mbed TLS error code into a human-readable string. Writes a textual description of errnum into buffer, truncating as needed, and guarantees a terminating null byte when buflen permits. Intended for turning return codes from Mbed TLS APIs (typically negative error codes) into messages for logs or diagnostics. The function returns no value; the caller inspects the contents of buffer after the call.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, writable memory region of at least buflen bytes.
buflen must be >= 1 to allow writing the terminating null byte; if smaller, output cannot be produced.
errnum should be an Mbed TLS error code as returned by Mbed TLS functions (commonly a negative value); non-recognized codes may yield a generic or unknown message.
Caller must not assume the full message fits; the output may be truncated to buflen - 1 characters plus the terminating null.
Thread-safe usage is allowed as the function only writes to the caller-provided buffer and does not require global state (inferred from signature and typical implementation).
The function does not report errors via return value; callers must rely solely on the contents of buffer.

functions.name: mbedtls_pkcs7_init
functions.description: Initialize an mbedtls_pkcs7 structure for subsequent parsing/verifying operations by setting its fields to a known, empty state. Typical usage: allocate an mbedtls_pkcs7 object (stack or heap), call mbedtls_pkcs7_init(), then mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der(), then verification functions, and finally mbedtls_pkcs7_free().
requirements: pkcs7 must be a valid, writable pointer to an mbedtls_pkcs7 object provided by the caller.
Call this function before any other operation on the pkcs7 object.
This function does not free memory; it only initializes the structure.

functions.name: mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der
functions.signature: int mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der(mbedtls_pkcs7 *pkcs7, const unsigned char *buf, const size_t buflen);
functions.description: Parse a single DER-encoded PKCS #7 detached signature and populate pkcs7. On success returns the mbedtls_pkcs7_type of the parsed content; on failure returns a negative error code. The implementation supports only the SignedData content type (version 1), DER encoding, and detached signatures; it internally copies the input buffer so the caller may release it after the call.
requirements: pkcs7 must point to an initialized mbedtls_pkcs7 structure (e.g., via mbedtls_pkcs7_init).
buf must point to a buffer containing exactly one DER-encoded PKCS #7 object; buflen must be exactly the encoded content length (no trailing data).
Only detached signatures are supported; inputs with embedded content are unsupported.
Only DER encoding is supported (BER is not accepted).
Only the SignedData content type is supported; other content types will fail with an error.
Only SignedData version 1 is supported.
The structure may include at most one X.509 certificate; certificates must be X.509 (no PKCS #6).
Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs), authenticated/unauthenticated attributes, and non-empty contentInfo are not supported and are assumed absent/empty.

On failure, a negative error code is returned (e.g., MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_FORMAT, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_VERSION, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_CONTENT_INFO, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_ALG, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_CERT, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_SIGNATURE, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_INVALID_SIGNER_INFO, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_BAD_INPUT_DATA, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_ALLOC_FAILED).

functions.name: mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_data_verify
functions.signature: int mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_data_verify(mbedtls_pkcs7 *pkcs7, const mbedtls_x509_crt *cert, const unsigned char *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: Verify a PKCS #7 SignedData detached signature against a caller-supplied certificate by hashing the provided data using the signer’s indicated digest algorithm and comparing against each signer’s signature in the PKCS #7 object. Verification succeeds if any signer’s signature matches. Certificates embedded in the PKCS #7 are not used and no trust-chain validation is performed. Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: pkcs7 must reference a PKCS #7 object previously parsed successfully via mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der and containing a SignedData detached signature.
cert must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_x509_crt containing a public key suitable for verifying the signer’s signature.
data must point to the exact plaintext bytes that were signed; datalen must be the length of data in bytes (data may be NULL only if datalen is 0).
The function computes the hash internally; no pre-hashing by the caller is required.
No certificate chain validation or use of certificates inside the PKCS #7 is performed; caller is responsible for any identity/authenticity checks beyond signature validity.
Returns 0 if verification succeeds for any signer; otherwise returns a negative error code (e.g., MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_VERIFY_FAIL, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_BAD_INPUT_DATA).

functions.name: mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_hash_verify
functions.signature: int mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_hash_verify(mbedtls_pkcs7 *pkcs7, const mbedtls_x509_crt *cert, const unsigned char *hash, size_t hashlen);
functions.description: Verify a PKCS #7 SignedData detached signature against a caller-supplied certificate using a caller-supplied precomputed hash. The function validates the signature for each signer using the signer’s indicated digest algorithm. Succeeds if any signer verifies. Embedded certificates are not used and no trust-chain validation is performed. Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: pkcs7 must reference a PKCS #7 object previously parsed successfully via mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der and containing a SignedData detached signature.
cert must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_x509_crt containing a public key suitable for verifying the signer’s signature.
hash must be the digest of the signed data computed with the exact digest algorithm indicated by the signer; hashlen must match that digest’s output size.
hash may be NULL only if hashlen is 0.
No certificate chain validation or use of certificates inside the PKCS #7 is performed; caller is responsible for any identity/authenticity checks beyond signature validity.
Returns 0 if verification succeeds for any signer; otherwise returns a negative error code (e.g., MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_VERIFY_FAIL, MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_BAD_INPUT_DATA).

functions.name: mbedtls_pkcs7_free
functions.description: Release and zeroize all resources held inside an mbedtls_pkcs7 structure. The structure itself is not freed; the caller owns it and may reuse it after calling mbedtls_pkcs7_init() again.
requirements: pkcs7 must be a valid pointer to an mbedtls_pkcs7 object (it is safe if the object was only initialized).
Call this after you are done with the pkcs7 object to avoid memory/resource leaks.
Do not use the pkcs7 object after this call unless it is re-initialized with mbedtls_pkcs7_init().

functions.name: mbedtls_version_get_number
functions.description: Returns the library’s version number encoded as an unsigned integer with format MMNNPP00 (Major, Minor, Patch). Use this to compare versions numerically at runtime without parsing strings.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return value encodes version as MMNNPP00 (e.g., 3.6.1 -> 03060100).
Caller should interpret the numeric format as MMNNPP00 for comparisons (do not assume any other packing).
Function is available only when the library is built with MBEDTLS_VERSION_C enabled.

functions.name: mbedtls_version_get_string
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a read-only, null-terminated C string representing the version as "x.y.z". Useful for logging or displaying the exact version at runtime.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to a read-only string (const); the caller must not modify the contents.
The returned pointer is expected to point to a valid, null-terminated string.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is not documented; treat it as non-owning and do not attempt to free it.
Function is available only when the library is built with MBEDTLS_VERSION_C enabled.

functions.name: mbedtls_version_get_string_full
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a read-only, null-terminated C string with the full version text, formatted like "Mbed TLS x.y.z". Intended for human-readable identification of the library version.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to a read-only string (const); the caller must not modify the contents.
The returned pointer is expected to point to a valid, null-terminated string.

Function is available only when the library is built with MBEDTLS_VERSION_C enabled.

functions.name: mbedtls_version_check_feature
functions.description: Checks at runtime whether a particular compile-time feature was enabled in the built library. Pass the name of a configuration macro (e.g., "MBEDTLS_SSL_SRV_C"). Returns 0 if present, -1 if absent, and -2 if feature-checking support is not compiled in.
requirements: feature must point to a valid, null-terminated C string naming a compile-time configuration macro (e.g., "MBEDTLS_SSL_SRV_C").
feature should not be NULL (not documented, but a valid string is required to perform the check).
Caller must handle return codes: 0 (present), -1 (not present), -2 (feature-checking not compiled in).
Function only checks macros from the sections "System support", "Mbed TLS modules", and "Mbed TLS feature support" in mbedtls_config.h, as documented.

def _interesting_oid_arcs(rng):
    preset = [
        [0, 0],            # minimal for first=0
        [0, 39, 0],        # boundary second arc
        [1, 0],            # minimal for first=1
        [1, 39, 39],       # boundary with extra arc
        [2, 0],            # minimal for first=2
        [2, 100],          # second arc >39 allowed for first=2

    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):

def der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0x80:
        return bytes([n])
    s = []
    tmp = n
    while tmp > 0:
        s.append(tmp & 0xFF)
        tmp >>= 8
    s.reverse()
    return bytes([0x80 | len(s)]) + bytes(s)


def der_oid(*arcs) -> bytes:

    body = [first]

        if a == 0:

        else:

            v = a
            while v > 0:
                stack.append(0x80 | (v & 0x7F))
                v >>= 7

def der_sequence(*elements: bytes) -> bytes:
    content = b"".join(elements)
    return bytes([0x30]) + der_len(len(content)) + content


def der_set(*elements: bytes) -> bytes:
    content = b"".join(elements)
    return bytes([0x31]) + der_len(len(content)) + content

# Common OIDs used in X.509
OIDS = {
    # Basic Constraints: 2.5.29.19
    'basicConstraints': (2, 5, 29, 19),
    # Key Usage: 2.5.29.15
    'keyUsage': (2, 5, 29, 15),
    # Extended Key Usage: 2.5.29.37
    'extKeyUsage': (2, 5, 29, 37),
    # SAN: 2.5.29.17
    'subjectAltName': (2, 5, 29, 17),
    # EKU OIDs
    'serverAuth': (1, 3, 6, 1, 5, 5, 7, 3, 1),
    'clientAuth': (1, 3, 6, 1, 5, 5, 7, 3, 2),
}

# Build valid extension value payloads (the content inside the OCTET STRING)

def ext_basic_constraints(ca: bool, pathlen: int | None) -> bytes:
    elems = [der_boolean(ca)]
    if ca and pathlen is not None:
        elems.append(der_integer(max(0, pathlen)))
    return der_sequence(*elems)


def ext_key_usage(flags: int) -> bytes:
    # Key Usage is BIT STRING; map flags into two bytes (common bits)
    # Bits: digitalSignature(0), nonRepudiation(1), keyEncipherment(2), dataEncipherment(3),
    # keyAgreement(4), keyCertSign(5), cRLSign(6), encipherOnly(7), decipherOnly(8)
    b0 = flags & 0xFF
    b1 = (flags >> 8) & 0xFF
    bs = bytes([b0]) + (bytes([b1]) if b1 else b"")
    return der_bit_string(bs, 0)


def ext_ext_key_usage(oids: list[tuple]) -> bytes:
    seq_elems = [der_oid(*arcs) for arcs in oids]
    return der_sequence(*seq_elems)

# SAN helper encoders

CONTEXT_SPECIFIC = {
    'otherName': 0xA0,
    'rfc822Name': 0x81,
    'dNSName': 0x82,
    'x400Address': 0x83,
    'directoryName': 0xA4,
    'ediPartyName': 0xA5,
    'uniformResourceIdentifier': 0x86,
    'iPAddress': 0x87,
    'registeredID': 0x88,
}


def der_explicit(tag: int, content: bytes) -> bytes:
    # tag is already context-specific constructed (e.g., 0xA0, 0xA4)
    return bytes([tag]) + der_len(len(content)) + content


def san_dns(name: str) -> bytes:
    b = name.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    return bytes([CONTEXT_SPECIFIC['dNSName']]) + der_len(len(b)) + b


def san_uri(uri: str) -> bytes:
    b = uri.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    return bytes([CONTEXT_SPECIFIC['uniformResourceIdentifier']]) + der_len(len(b)) + b


def san_ip(ip: str) -> bytes:
    try:
        ip_obj = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
        b = ip_obj.packed
    except ValueError:
        # fallback to 127.0.0.1
        b = ipaddress.ip_address('127.0.0.1').packed
    return bytes([CONTEXT_SPECIFIC['iPAddress']]) + der_len(len(b)) + b


def san_dirname_cn(cn: str) -> bytes:
    # directoryName is an X.509 Name (SEQUENCE of RDNs (SET of AttributeTypeValue))
    # Build Name with one RDN: CN=<cn>
    oid_cn = (2, 5, 4, 3)
    atv = der_sequence(der_oid(*oid_cn), bytes([0x0C]) + der_len(len(cn.encode())) + cn.encode())  # UTF8String
    rdn = der_set(atv)
    name = der_sequence(rdn)
    return der_explicit(CONTEXT_SPECIFIC['directoryName'], name)


def ext_subject_alt_name(entries: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # SAN value is a SEQUENCE of GeneralName
    return der_sequence(*entries)

# OID generation pool

COMMON_OIDS = [
    OIDS['basicConstraints'],
    OIDS['keyUsage'],
    OIDS['extKeyUsage'],
    OIDS['subjectAltName'],
    OIDS['serverAuth'],
    OIDS['clientAuth'],
]


def random_der_oid(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rnd.randrange(0, 6)
    if choice < len(COMMON_OIDS):
        return der_oid(*COMMON_OIDS[choice])
    # random valid-looking OID
    first = rnd.choice([0, 1, 2])
    second = rnd.randrange(0, 40)
    rest_len = rnd.randrange(0, 6)
    rest = [rnd.randrange(0, 2**21) for _ in range(rest_len)]
    return der_oid(first, second, *rest)


def make_extension_pair(rnd: random.Random) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    # Returns (oid_bytes, value_bytes_inside_octet_string)
    kind = rnd.randrange(0, 4)
    if kind == 0:
        # basicConstraints
        ca = rnd.choice([True, False])
        pathlen = rnd.choice([None, 0, 1, 3]) if ca else None
        val = ext_basic_constraints(ca, pathlen)
        return der_oid(*OIDS['basicConstraints']), val
    elif kind == 1:
        # keyUsage
        # choose a few meaningful combinations
        combos = [
            0x80,              # decipherOnly (bit 7 of first byte) - uncommon but permitted
            0x20 | 0x02 | 0x01,  # keyCertSign | nonRepudiation | digitalSignature
            0x04 | 0x08,       # keyEncipherment | dataEncipherment
            0x10 | 0x01,       # keyAgreement | digitalSignature
        ]
        flags = rnd.choice(combos)
        val = ext_key_usage(flags)
        return der_oid(*OIDS['keyUsage']), val
    elif kind == 2:
        # extKeyUsage with common EKUs
        oids = [OIDS['serverAuth'], OIDS['clientAuth']]
        rnd.shuffle(oids)
        val = ext_ext_key_usage(oids[: rnd.randrange(1, len(oids) + 1)])
        return der_oid(*OIDS['extKeyUsage']), val
    else:
        # subjectAltName with 1-3 entries
        entries = []
        for _ in range(1, rnd.randrange(2, 4)):
            t = rnd.randrange(0, 4)
            if t == 0:
                entries.append(san_dns('www.example.com'))
            elif t == 1:
                entries.append(san_uri('https://example.com/service'))
            elif t == 2:
                entries.append(san_ip('2001:db8::1'))
            else:
                entries.append(san_dirname_cn('CN-Alt'))
        val = ext_subject_alt_name(entries)
        return der_oid(*OIDS['subjectAltName']), val


def pack_fields(fields: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate fields with small random separators that are also valid standalone data.
    # Use a single zero-length separator or a single ASCII as minimal noise to avoid breaking consumers.
    out = bytearray()
    sep = b"\x00"
    for i, f in enumerate(fields):
        out += f
        if i + 1 < len(fields):
            out += sep
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    blobs: list[bytes] = []

    # 1) Provide several valid DER OIDs for APIs expecting OID buffers (including EKU check)
    for _ in range(3):
        blobs.append(random_der_oid(rnd))

    # 2) Provide extension OID + value pairs suitable for *_set_extension and *_set_subject_alternative_name
    for _ in range(3):
        oid, val = make_extension_pair(rnd)
        blobs.append(oid)
        # For set_extension, value must be the raw value INSIDE the OCTET STRING, so provide val directly
        blobs.append(val)

    # 3) Also include a couple of short raw buffers for cases where stub trims/resizes arbitrarily
    blobs.append(b"\x55\x04\x03")  # AttributeType OID prefix (2.5.4.3) fragment
    blobs.append(b"DNS:example.org")

    # 4) Include a plausible EKU OID buffer again for mbedtls_x509_crt_check_extended_key_usage
    blobs.append(der_oid(*OIDS['serverAuth']))

    # Ensure size limit
    payload = pack_fields(blobs)
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]
    return payload

# Target data type: DER-encoded extension value (the inner bytes that go inside
# the OCTET STRING of an X.509 extension). The fuzz stubs also request arbitrary
# OID byte strings (FUZZ_PARAM_STR) and various blobs used by SSL session/cache
# helpers. We'll generate a single bytes buffer that concatenates several
# self-contained items separated by simple length prefixes so that the fuzzing
# harness can slice them as needed.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a sequence of TLV-like chunks that are valid and interesting for
#   X.509/ASN.1 consumers:
#   * Common extensions with realistic DER for their inner value (e.g.,
#     BasicConstraints, KeyUsage, ExtendedKeyUsage, SubjectAltName).
#   * Provide corresponding OIDs as separate chunks to pair with values in
#     set_extension fuzzers.
# - Also include generic random blobs for SSL session/cache inputs and PRF.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Chunk encoding used here (simple framing for multiple buffers in one bytestream):
#   [2-byte big-endian length][payload bytes]
# The fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; typical harnesses pick
# successive slices. This framing makes each call receive a coherent payload.

# Helper: simple DER builders for a few extension inner values

def der_boolean(val: bool) -> bytes:
    return b"\x01\x01" + (b"\xff" if val else b"\x00")

def der_integer(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimal two's-complement encoding
    if n == 0:
        enc = b"\x00"
    else:
        out = bytearray()
        v = n
        while v > 0:
            out.append(v & 0xFF)
            v >>= 8
        out = bytes(reversed(out))
        if out[0] & 0x80:
            out = b"\x00" + out
        enc = out
    return b"\x02" + bytes([len(enc)]) + enc

def der_bit_string(bits: bytes, unused_bits: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return b"\x03" + bytes([len(bits) + 1]) + bytes([unused_bits]) + bits

def der_octet_string(val: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x04" + der_len(len(val)) + val

def der_oid_from_arcs(arcs):
    # arcs: list of integers, e.g., [2,5,29,19]
    if len(arcs) < 2:
        arcs = [1, 3] + list(arcs)
    first = 40 * arcs[0] + arcs[1]
    body = bytes([first]) + b"".join(der_base128(x) for x in arcs[2:])
    return b"\x06" + der_len(len(body)) + body

def der_base128(x: int) -> bytes:
    # Encode non-negative integer in base-128, MSB continuation bits
    if x == 0:
        return b"\x00"
    tmp = []
    while x > 0:
        tmp.append(x & 0x7F)
        x >>= 7
    out = bytearray()
    for i, v in enumerate(reversed(tmp)):
        if i != len(tmp) - 1:
            out.append(0x80 | v)
        else:
            out.append(v)
    return bytes(out)

def der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0x80:
        return bytes([n])
    s = []
    v = n
    while v:
        s.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 8
    s = bytes(reversed(s))
    return bytes([0x80 | len(s)]) + s

def der_sequence(content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x30" + der_len(len(content)) + content

def der_set(content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x31" + der_len(len(content)) + content

# Specific X.509 extension inner encoders (content to be wrapped in OCTET STRING)

def ext_basic_constraints(is_ca: bool, pathlen: int | None) -> bytes:
    seq = der_boolean(is_ca)
    if pathlen is not None and pathlen >= 0:
        seq += der_integer(pathlen)
    return der_sequence(seq)

def ext_key_usage(flags: int) -> bytes:
    # BIT STRING; map lower 9 bits (ignore decipherOnly high bit which CSR API can't set)
    # We pack bits little-endian within bytes as in DER (msb first, but bit 0 is LSB of first octet when reading semantics)
    # For DER, bits are presented MSB-first; here we just place the raw bitmap bytes.
    # Compute minimal number of bytes
    bits_len = 0
    tmp = flags
    while tmp:
        bits_len += 1
        tmp >>= 8
    bits_len = max(bits_len, 1)
    bit_bytes = flags.to_bytes(bits_len, 'big')
    # Calculate unused bits in final octet to have clean boundary
    total_bits = bits_len * 8
    highest_bit = flags.bit_length() or 1
    unused = (8 - (highest_bit % 8)) % 8
    return der_bit_string(bit_bytes, unused)

def ext_ext_key_usage(oids:list[tuple[int,...]]) -> bytes:
    content = b"".join(der_oid_from_arcs(oid) for oid in oids)
    return der_sequence(content)

def ext_subject_alt_name(dns:list[str], uris:list[str], ips:list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # GeneralName: [2] dNSName (IA5String), [6] uniformResourceIdentifier, [7] iPAddress (OCTET STRING raw bytes)
    out = bytearray()
    for d in dns:
        ia5 = d.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
        out += bytes([0x82]) + der_len(len(ia5)) + ia5  # [2] IA5String implicit -> tag 0x82 (context-specific primitive)
    for u in uris:
        ia5 = u.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
        out += bytes([0x86]) + der_len(len(ia5)) + ia5  # [6]
    for ip in ips:
        out += bytes([0x87]) + der_len(len(ip)) + ip    # [7]
    return der_sequence(bytes(out))

def make_valid_oid_and_value_pairs(rnd: random.Random) -> list[tuple[bytes, bytes]]:
    pairs = []
    # OIDs (arcs) for common extensions: id-ce-(basicConstraints=19, keyUsage=15, extKeyUsage=37, subjectAltName=17)
    id_ce = (2,5,29)
    pairs.append((der_oid_from_arcs(id_ce + (19,)), ext_basic_constraints(rnd.choice([True, False]), rnd.choice([None, 0, 1, 3]))))
    # KeyUsage flags selection
    ku_candidates = [
        0x80,                                 # digitalSignature
        0x20,                                 # keyEncipherment
        0x04,                                 # keyCertSign
        0x02 | 0x20,                          # nonRepudiation|keyEncipherment
        0xFF & 0x7F                           # many bits within 1 byte (exclude decipherOnly high bit beyond 1 byte)
    ]
    pairs.append((der_oid_from_arcs(id_ce + (15,)), ext_key_usage(rnd.choice(ku_candidates))))
    # ExtendedKeyUsage: serverAuth(1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1), clientAuth(…3.2)
    eku_server = (1,3,6,1,5,5,7,3,1)
    eku_client = (1,3,6,1,5,5,7,3,2)
    sel = []
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        sel.append(eku_server)
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        sel.append(eku_client)
    if not sel:
        sel = [eku_server]
    pairs.append((der_oid_from_arcs(id_ce + (37,)), ext_ext_key_usage(sel)))
    # SubjectAltName: include a mix of DNS, URI, IP
    dns_samples = ["example.com", "test.local", "xn--d1acpjx3f.xn--p1ai"]
    uri_samples = ["https://example.com/api", "spiffe://trust-domain/service"]
    ipv4 = bytes([rnd.randint(1, 254) for _ in range(4)])
    ipv6 = bytes([rnd.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(16)])
    san = ext_subject_alt_name(
        dns=[rnd.choice(dns_samples)],
        uris=[rnd.choice(uri_samples)] if rnd.random() < 0.5 else [],
        ips=[ipv4] + ([ipv6] if rnd.random() < 0.5 else [])
    )
    pairs.append((der_oid_from_arcs(id_ce + (17,)), san))
    return pairs

# Additional blobs for other stubs

def make_ssl_session_blob(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce a plausible serialized session-like blob, but not tied to real format
    # Keep variable length to exercise paths.
    length = rnd.randint(32, 256)
    return rnd.randbytes(length)

def make_psk_and_identity(rnd: random.Random) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    psk_len = rnd.randint(1, 64)
    id_len  = rnd.randint(0, 64)
    psk = rnd.randbytes(psk_len)
    identity = rnd.randbytes(id_len)
    return psk, identity

def make_tls_prf_inputs(rnd: random.Random) -> tuple[bytes, bytes, bytes, int]:
    secret = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(16, 64))
    label_choices = [b"extended master secret", b"key expansion", b"exporter"]
    label = rnd.choice(label_choices)
    random_bytes = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(8, 64))
    out_len = rnd.randint(0, 256)
    return secret, label, random_bytes, out_len

# Framing helper

def frame(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", len(payload)) + payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    chunks: list[bytes] = []

    # 1) Provide several OID/value pairs for x509write_*_set_extension fuzzers
    for oid, inner in make_valid_oid_and_value_pairs(rnd):
        # The fuzzer supplies OID bytes and separately supplies the inner value bytes.
        # We emit both as independent framed blobs so successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
        # get meaningful data.
        chunks.append(frame(oid))
        chunks.append(frame(inner))
        # Also include the same inner value wrapped in OCTET STRING (some code paths might expect it)
        chunks.append(frame(der_octet_string(inner)))

    # 2) Add a few random-but-well-formed DER payload varieties to diversify
    #    - An INTEGER, a BOOLEAN, and an empty SEQUENCE
    chunks.append(frame(der_integer(rnd.randint(0, 2**32 - 1))))
    chunks.append(frame(der_boolean(rnd.choice([True, False]))))
    chunks.append(frame(der_sequence(b"")))

    # 3) SSL session/cache and context loaders: add arbitrary blobs
    for _ in range(3):
        chunks.append(frame(make_ssl_session_blob(rnd)))

    # 4) PSK and identity for mbedtls_ssl_conf_psk
    psk, identity = make_psk_and_identity(rnd)
    chunks.append(frame(psk))
    chunks.append(frame(identity))

    # 5) PRF inputs
    secret, label, random_bytes, out_len = make_tls_prf_inputs(rnd)
    chunks.append(frame(secret))
    chunks.append(frame(label))
    chunks.append(frame(random_bytes))
    chunks.append(frame(struct.pack('>H', out_len)))

    # 6) Client transport ID buffer (arbitrary bytes)
    chunks.append(frame(rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(0, 64))))

    # 7) Cache session IDs (1..32 bytes), add a couple
    for _ in range(2):
        sid_len = rnd.randint(1, 32)
        chunks.append(frame(rnd.randbytes(sid_len)))

    # Cap total size to 4096
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    return out[:4096]

import random
import struct
import time

# This generator produces a small, valid X.509 certificate in DER form.
# It builds a self-signed v1 RSA certificate with minimal fields and a
# dummy public key (all-zero modulus is non-functional but DER-valid).
# The goal is to exercise mbedtls_x509_crt_parse_der / _parse with valid ASN.1.
# Size kept << 4096.

def _len_bytes(length: int) -> bytes:
    if length < 0x80:
        return bytes([length])
    # Long-form length
    out = []
    while length > 0:
        out.append(length & 0xFF)
        length >>= 8
    out.reverse()
    return bytes([0x80 | len(out)]) + bytes(out)

def _seq(content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x30" + _len_bytes(len(content)) + content

def _set(content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x31" + _len_bytes(len(content)) + content

def _int(i: int) -> bytes:
    # Encode non-negative INTEGER
    if i == 0:
        body = b"\x00"
    else:
        body = bytearray()
        while i > 0:
            body.insert(0, i & 0xFF)
            i >>= 8
        # Ensure positive (add leading 0x00 if high bit set)
        if body[0] & 0x80:
            body.insert(0, 0)
        body = bytes(body)
    return b"\x02" + _len_bytes(len(body)) + body

def _bool(v: bool) -> bytes:
    return b"\x01\x01" + (b"\xFF" if v else b"\x00")

def _bit_string(bits: bytes, unused_bits: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return b"\x03" + _len_bytes(len(bits) + 1) + bytes([unused_bits]) + bits

def _octet_string(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x04" + _len_bytes(len(b)) + b

def _oid(oid: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode dotted OID
    parts = [int(x) for x in oid.split('.')]
    if len(parts) < 2:
        raise ValueError("OID needs at least two arcs")
    first = 40 * parts[0] + parts[1]
    body = bytearray()
    def enc_arc(n: int):
        tmp = []
        if n == 0:
            tmp = [0]
        else:
            while n > 0:
                tmp.append(n & 0x7F)
                n >>= 7
        tmp.reverse()
        for i, b7 in enumerate(tmp):
            body.append((0x80 | b7) if i < len(tmp) - 1 else b7)
    enc_arc(first)
    for p in parts[2:]:
        enc_arc(p)
    return b"\x06" + _len_bytes(len(body)) + bytes(body)

def _utc_time(t: time.struct_time) -> bytes:
    # YYMMDDhhmmssZ
    year = t.tm_year % 100
    s = f"{year:02d}{t.tm_mon:02d}{t.tm_mday:02d}{t.tm_hour:02d}{t.tm_min:02d}{t.tm_sec:02d}Z"
    b = s.encode('ascii')
    return b"\x17" + _len_bytes(len(b)) + b

def _printable_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return b"\x13" + _len_bytes(len(b)) + b

def _ia5_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return b"\x16" + _len_bytes(len(b)) + b

def _context(tag: int, content: bytes, constructed: bool = True) -> bytes:
    t = 0xA0 + tag if constructed else 0x80 + tag
    return bytes([t]) + _len_bytes(len(content)) + content

# Build Name (X.509): Name ::= SEQUENCE OF RDNs; each RDN = SET of AttributeTypeAndValue
# We'll include CN and O to vary some content.

def _attr(oid: str, value: bytes) -> bytes:
    return _seq(_oid(oid) + value)

def _rdn_set(atv: bytes) -> bytes:
    return _set(atv)

def _name(cn: str, org: str | None) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    parts.append(_rdn_set(_attr("2.5.4.3", _printable_string(cn))))  # CN
    if org:
        parts.append(_rdn_set(_attr("2.5.4.10", _printable_string(org))))  # O
    return _seq(b"".join(parts))

# AlgorithmIdentifier for sha256WithRSAEncryption: 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 with NULL params

def _alg_sha256_rsa() -> bytes:
    return _seq(_oid("1.2.840.113549.1.1.11") + b"\x05\x00")

# SubjectPublicKeyInfo with rsaEncryption and a tiny modulus/exponent
# rsaEncryption: 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1 with NULL params

def _spki_rsa(modulus_bytes: bytes, exp: int = 65537) -> bytes:
    alg = _seq(_oid("1.2.840.113549.1.1.1") + b"\x05\x00")
    rsa_seq = _seq(_int(int.from_bytes(modulus_bytes, 'big')) + _int(exp))
    bitstr = _bit_string(rsa_seq)
    return _seq(alg + bitstr)

# SignatureValue: BIT STRING; we place a small deterministic dummy

def _dummy_signature(length: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a sequence of bytes and wrap in bit string
    sig = bytes((i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF for i in range(length))
    return _bit_string(sig)


def _tbs_cert(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # version v1 (explicit [0] default 0). We'll include it explicitly: [0] EXPLICIT Version
    version = _context(0, _int(0))

    # serial number: random 64-bit positive int
    serial = _int(rnd.getrandbits(64) | 1)

    # signature algorithm
    sigalg = _alg_sha256_rsa()

    # issuer / subject
    cn_list = ["Fuzz Cert", "Test Node", "MbedTLS", "Example"]
    org_list = ["Acme", "Contoso", "Widgets", "Example Org", None]
    cn_issuer = rnd.choice(cn_list)
    org_issuer = rnd.choice(org_list)
    issuer = _name(cn_issuer, org_issuer)

    cn_subject = rnd.choice(cn_list)
    org_subject = rnd.choice(org_list)
    subject = _name(cn_subject, org_subject)

    # validity: notBefore and notAfter (UTC time)
    now = time.gmtime(int(time.time()))
    # notBefore = now - delta days, notAfter = now + delta days
    delta_days = 30 + rnd.randrange(0, 365)
    before_ts = int(time.time()) - delta_days * 86400

    # SubjectPublicKeyInfo: use 256-bit modulus content to keep size small
    mod = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(32))

    spki = _spki_rsa(mod)

    tbs = _seq(version + serial + sigalg + issuer + validity + subject + spki)
    return tbs
