import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid PEM-encoded X.509 certificate buffers.
# It embeds a small, DER-encoded TBSCertificate/Certificate with a NULL signature
# algorithm and an empty signature (for simplicity and to keep size small). While
# not cryptographically valid, mbedtls_x509_crt_parse accepts some self-contained
# minimal DER structures for parsing various paths; however, to improve validity
# we construct syntactically valid ASN.1 structures and wrap them into PEM.
# The fuzzer stub sometimes wraps our bytes into a PEM envelope anyway; to
# satisfy both paths, we directly return a proper PEM with correct base64 and
# NUL terminator. The stub will copy it and use the PEM codepath.

# ASN.1 helpers

def asn1_len(length: int) -> bytes:
    if length < 0x80:
        return bytes([length])
    # long-form
    tmp = []
    v = length
    while v > 0:
        tmp.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 1 << 3
    tmp.reverse()
    return bytes([0x80 | len(tmp)]) + bytes(tmp)

def asn1_tag(tag: int, content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return bytes([tag]) + asn1_len(len(content)) + content

def asn1_boolean(val: bool) -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x01, b"\xFF" if val else b"\x00")

def asn1_integer(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Encode non-negative integer
    if n == 0:
        content = b"\x00"
    else:
        out = bytearray()
        v = n
        while v > 0:
            out.append(v & 0xFF)
            v >>= 8
        out.reverse()
        # Ensure first bit not interpreted as sign
        if out[0] & 0x80:
            out = bytearray(b"\x00") + out
        content = bytes(out)
    return asn1_tag(0x02, content)

def asn1_bit_string(bits: bytes, unused_bits: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x03, bytes([unused_bits]) + bits)

def asn1_octet_string(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x04, data)

def asn1_null() -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x05, b"")

def asn1_oid(oid_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x06, oid_bytes)

def asn1_utctime(y: int, mo: int, d: int, h: int, mi: int, s: int) -> bytes:
    # UTCTime YYMMDDhhmmssZ with two-digit year
    yy = y % 100
    txt = f"{yy:02d}{mo:02d}{d:02d}{h:02d}{mi:02d}{s:02d}Z".encode()
    return asn1_tag(0x17, txt)

def asn1_gentime(y: int, mo: int, d: int, h: int, mi: int, s: int) -> bytes:
    txt = f"{y:04d}{mo:02d}{d:02d}{h:02d}{mi:02d}{s:02d}Z".encode()
    return asn1_tag(0x18, txt)

def asn1_sequence(content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x30, content)

def asn1_set(content: bytes) -> bytes:
    return asn1_tag(0x31, content)

def asn1_explicit(tag_no: int, content: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Context-specific constructed [tag_no]
    return asn1_tag(0xA0 + tag_no, content)

# OIDs encoded per DER (first two arcs: 1*40 + 2, etc.)
OID_RSA_ENC = b"\x2a\x86\x48\x86\xf7\x0d\x01\x01\x01"  # 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1 rsaEncryption
OID_SHA256_RSA = b"\x2a\x86\x48\x86\xf7\x0d\x01\x01\x0b"  # 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 sha256WithRSAEncryption
OID_CN = b"\x55\x04\x03"  # 2.5.4.3 commonName
OID_C = b"\x55\x04\x06"   # 2.5.4.6 countryName
OID_O = b"\x55\x04\x0a"   # 2.5.4.10 organizationName


def name_rdn_sequence(common_name: str, country: str, org: str) -> bytes:
    # RDNSequence ::= SEQUENCE OF RDN; RDN ::= SET OF AttributeTypeAndValue
    atv_cn = asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(OID_CN) + asn1_tag(0x0C, common_name.encode()))  # UTF8String
    atv_c = asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(OID_C) + asn1_tag(0x13, country.encode()))       # PrintableString
    atv_o = asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(OID_O) + asn1_tag(0x0C, org.encode()))
    rdn1 = asn1_set(atv_c)
    rdn2 = asn1_set(atv_o)
    rdn3 = asn1_set(atv_cn)
    return asn1_sequence(rdn1 + rdn2 + rdn3)


def subject_public_key_info_rsa(mod_bits: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimal, synthetic RSA key: modulus with one set bit, exponent 65537
    n_bytes = (mod_bits + 7) // 8
    # Create a modulus with high bit set and otherwise random-looking but valid length
    n = bytearray(b"\x80" + bytes(max(0, n_bytes - 1)))
    # INTEGERs must be positive; leading 0x00 added if top bit set, but we already ensure 0x80 then DER requires a 0x00 prefix
    n_int = asn1_integer(int.from_bytes(b"\x01" + b"\x00" * (n_bytes - 1), "big"))
    e_int = asn1_integer(65537)
    rsa_pub = asn1_sequence(n_int + e_int)
    alg = asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(OID_RSA_ENC) + asn1_null())
    return asn1_sequence(alg + asn1_bit_string(rsa_pub, 0))


def validity_dates(start_year: int, span_days: int) -> bytes:
    # Use UTCTime for <= 2049 start year; NotBefore <= NotAfter
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta
    nb = datetime(start_year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    na = nb + timedelta(days=span_days)
    # Use UTCTime for both to stay small
    nb_asn1 = asn1_utctime(nb.year, nb.month, nb.day, nb.hour, nb.minute, nb.second)
    na_asn1 = asn1_utctime(na.year, na.month, na.day, na.hour, na.minute, na.second)
    return asn1_sequence(nb_asn1 + na_asn1)


def minimal_cert(common_name: str, country: str, org: str, serial: int, mod_bits: int,
                  is_ca: bool, not_before_year: int, validity_days: int) -> bytes:
    # tbsCertificate
    version = asn1_explicit(0, asn1_integer(2))  # v3
    serial_num = asn1_integer(serial)
    sig_alg = asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(OID_SHA256_RSA) + asn1_null())
    issuer = name_rdn_sequence(common_name + " Issuer", country, org)
    validity = validity_dates(not_before_year, validity_days)
    subject = name_rdn_sequence(common_name, country, org)
    spki = subject_public_key_info_rsa(mod_bits)

    # BasicConstraints CA if desired
    ext_list: List[bytes] = []
    if is_ca:
        bc = asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(b"\x55\x1d\x13") +  # 2.5.29.19 basicConstraints
                           asn1_boolean(True))
        ext_list.append(asn1_sequence(asn1_oid(b"\x55\x1d\x13") + asn1_boolean(True) + asn1_octet_string(asn1_sequence(asn1_boolean(True)))))
    if ext_list:
        extensions = asn1_explicit(3, asn1_sequence(b"".join(ext_list)))
    else:
        extensions = b""

    tbs = asn1_sequence(version + serial_num + sig_alg + issuer + validity + subject + spki + extensions)
    # Outer Certificate = SEQUENCE { tbsCertificate, signatureAlgorithm, signatureValue }
    outer_sig_alg = sig_alg
    signature = asn1_bit_string(b"\x00")  # empty signature value (0 unused bits + 0 content)
    cert = asn1_sequence(tbs + outer_sig_alg + signature)
    return cert


def der_to_pem(der: bytes) -> bytes:
    b64 = base64.encodebytes(der).replace(b"\n", b"\n")
    # Wrap at 64 columns
    b64_str = base64.b64encode(der).decode()
    lines = [b64_str[i:i+64] for i in range(0, len(b64_str), 64)]
    body = "\n".join(lines)
    pem = f"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n{body}\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n".encode()
    return pem


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose parameters to explore parser paths
    common_names = [
        "Fuzz Test Leaf",
        "mbedTLS Example",
        "Local Test CA",
        "Long CN " + ("A" * rnd.randint(1, 32)),
    ]
    orgs = ["Acme Corp", "Example Org", "Test Org", "DevOps"]
    countries = ["US", "GB", "DE", "FR", "JP"]

    cn = rnd.choice(common_names)
    org = rnd.choice(orgs)
    c = rnd.choice(countries)
    serial = rnd.randint(1, (1 << 63) - 1)
    mod_bits = rnd.choice([512, 600, 768])  # keep small, within 4096 total size
    is_ca = rnd.choice([False, True])
    not_before_year = rnd.choice([2010, 2015, 2020])
    validity_days = rnd.choice([365, 3650])

    der = minimal_cert(cn, c, org, serial, mod_bits, is_ca, not_before_year, validity_days)

    # Optionally concatenate multiple PEM certs to exercise PEM multi-cert path
    count = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.7 else rnd.randint(2, 3)
    pems: List[bytes] = []
    for i in range(count):
        # vary CN slightly for subsequent certs
        der_i = der if i == 0 else minimal_cert(cn + f" #{i}", c, org, serial + i, mod_bits, is_ca, not_before_year, validity_days)
        pems.append(der_to_pem(der_i))
    out = b"".join(pems)

    # Ensure size limit and add NUL terminator for PEM parser requirement in stub
    if len(out) > 4000:
        out = out[:4000]
        # Truncate safely to line boundary if possible
        last_newline = out.rfind(b"\n")
        if last_newline > 0:
            out = out[:last_newline+1]
    return out + b"\x00"

from typing import List

# Target data type: hostname string
# Used by stubs:
# - mbedtls_x509_crt_verify, mbedtls_x509_crt_verify_with_profile: optional CN string (<=64)
# - mbedtls_ssl_ciphersuite_from_string / _get_ciphersuite_id: arbitrary C-string; not necessarily hostname, but our generator can still provide strings
# - mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname: hostname string (<= ~200)
# - Other stubs accept arbitrary strings; valid hostnames remain acceptable
#
# Strategy:
# Generate realistic, valid hostnames covering interesting cases:
# - simple domain (example.com)
# - multi-label domains with varying label counts and lengths
# - labels with digits and hyphens respecting RFC constraints (no leading/trailing hyphen, 1..63 chars)
# - punycode-like prefix (xn--) to exercise IDNA handling if present upstream
# - trailing dot (FQDN) variant
# - single-label hostnames (localhost, router)
# - IPv4/IPv6 textual forms (some consumers may accept IPs for CN checks)
# - wildcard patterns like *.example.com
# The buffer is a single bytes object containing one hostname. Fuzzer infra may reuse it for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# Keep size <= 4096.

ALPHA = string.ascii_lowercase
ALNUM = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits

COMMON_TLDS = [
    "com","net","org","io","dev","local","test","example","edu","gov"
]

COMMON_SLD = [
    "example","mbedtls","test","server","client","api","auth","cdn","mail","vpn","db","edge"
]

SINGLE_LABELS = ["localhost", "router", "gateway", "intranet", "host"]

CIPHERSUITE_LIKE = [
    # Some known names to help the ciphersuite-from-string stub find a match if present in build
    "TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",
    "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384",
    "TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",
    "TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",
    "TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",
]


def _label(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 20) -> str:
    ln = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # RFC: label must start and end with alnum; hyphens allowed inside
    if ln == 1:
        return rng.choice(ALNUM)
    # ensure first/last alnum
    first = rng.choice(ALNUM)
    last = rng.choice(ALNUM)
    mid_len = max(0, ln - 2)
    mid_chars = ALNUM + "-"
    mid = "".join(rng.choice(mid_chars) for _ in range(mid_len))
    # avoid consecutive dots or invalid hyphen positions already handled by constraining first/last
    return first + mid + last


def _random_domain(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose 2-5 labels
    n = rng.randint(2, 5)
    labels: List[str] = []
    for i in range(n):
        if i == n - 1:
            # TLD
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                labels.append(rng.choice(COMMON_TLDS))
            else:
                labels.append(_label(rng, 2, 6))
        elif i == 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
            labels.append(rng.choice(COMMON_SLD))
        else:
            # 1..20 length labels
            labels.append(_label(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 20)))
    return ".".join(labels)


def _punycode_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _label(rng, 2, 10)
    # Add xn-- prefix to first label to mimic IDNA punycode prefix
    return "xn--" + base + "." + rng.choice(COMMON_SLD) + "." + rng.choice(COMMON_TLDS)


def _wildcard_domain(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    dom = _random_domain(rng)
    # Prepend wildcard to first label only
    parts = dom.split(".")
    parts[0] = "*"
    return ".".join(parts)


def _ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return ".".join(str(rng.randint(0, 255)) for _ in range(4))


def _ipv6(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a simple full/shortened IPv6 string; not exhaustive but valid forms
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # full 8 groups
        return ":".join(f"{rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF):x}" for _ in range(8))
    else:
        # with :: compression
        left = rng.randint(1, 6)
        right = rng.randint(1, 7 - left)
        left_part = ":".join(f"{rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF):x}" for _ in range(left))
        right_part = ":".join(f"{rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF):x}" for _ in range(right))
        return left_part + "::" + right_part


def _maybe_trailing_dot(rng: random.Random, host: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        return host + "."
    return host


def _maybe_port(rng: random.Random, host: str) -> str:
    # Some consumers might pass raw hostnames; adding :port is sometimes accepted; keep probability low
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        return f"{host}:{rng.randint(1, 65535)}"
    return host


def _pick_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.15:
        host = rng.choice(SINGLE_LABELS)
    elif choice < 0.35:
        host = _random_domain(rng)
    elif choice < 0.50:
        host = _punycode_like(rng)
    elif choice < 0.65:
        host = _wildcard_domain(rng)
    elif choice < 0.80:
        host = _ipv4(rng)
    elif choice < 0.95:
        host = _ipv6(rng)
    else:
        # Sometimes provide a ciphersuite-like name to satisfy ciphersuite lookup stub
        host = rng.choice(CIPHERSUITE_LIKE)
    host = _maybe_trailing_dot(rng, host)
    host = _maybe_port(rng, host)
    # Bound length for different consumers: CN expects <=64; hostname setter allows ~200
    max_len = rng.choice([64, 120, 200])
    if len(host) > max_len:
        host = host[:max_len]
    return host


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    host = _pick_hostname(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and ASCII
    if not host:
        host = "example.com"
    # Encode to bytes; ASCII-safe
    data = host.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    # Guarantee NUL-termination safety by not including NUL in data; fuzzer infra passes as std::string
    # Limit size to 4096
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import struct
import string

# Target data type: DNS name string used in X.509 SAN dnsName entries.
# The fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to populate unstructured_name buffers
# for SAN, and also build minimal SAN lists from that string. We should therefore
# generate valid, interesting DNS names that exercise typical and edge cases while
# remaining valid.
#
# Constraints for a valid DNS name (RFC 1035/1123):
# - Consists of labels separated by dots.
# - Each label 1..63 chars; total length <= 253 chars (without trailing dot).
# - Labels: letters, digits, hyphen; must not start or end with a hyphen.
# - Case-insensitive; may include uppercase.
# - Internationalized names appear as A-labels (punycode) starting with xn--, we
#   can include such prefixes in ASCII to stay valid.
#
# We produce a mix of:
# - Simple hostnames (single label)
# - Multi-label FQDNs with varying label lengths
# - Names with numeric labels, hyphens inside, uppercase, trailing dot variant
# - Punycode-looking labels (xn--...)
# - Wildcard dNSName ("*.example.com") which is valid in certificates and often
#   handled specially.
#
# The stub may truncate to 64/128 bytes; we keep under 200 bytes.

ALPHA = string.ascii_lowercase
ALPHANUM = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
ALPHANUM_UP = string.ascii_letters + string.digits


def _rand_label(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 20) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # ensure first and last are alphanum, interior can include '-'
    if L == 1:
        return rng.choice(ALPHANUM)
    interior_len = L - 2
    interior_chars = ALPHANUM + "-"
    first = rng.choice(ALPHANUM)
    last = rng.choice(ALPHANUM)
    interior = ''.join(rng.choice(interior_chars) for _ in range(interior_len))
    # Avoid sequences like "--" at ends; interior can be anything
    return first + interior + last


def _rand_label_puny(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate an ASCII A-label that looks like punycode: xn-- + valid tail
    tail_len = rng.randint(1, 20)
    tail_chars = ALPHANUM + "-"
    tail = ''.join(rng.choice(tail_chars) for _ in range(tail_len))
    # Ensure it doesn't end with '-' to keep label valid
    if tail.endswith('-'):
        tail = tail[:-1] + rng.choice(ALPHANUM)
    return "xn--" + tail


def _rand_domain(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.randint(0, 7)
    labels = []
    if mode == 0:
        # simple hostname
        labels = [_rand_label(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 10))]
    elif mode == 1:
        # typical www.example.tld
        labels = ["www", _rand_label(rng, 3, 10), rng.choice(["com", "net", "org", "io", "dev"])]
    elif mode == 2:
        # deep subdomain
        depth = rng.randint(3, 6)
        labels = [_rand_label(rng, 1, 12) for _ in range(depth - 1)] + [rng.choice(["com", "net", "org", "edu", "gov"])]
    elif mode == 3:
        # include punycode-looking label
        labels = [_rand_label(rng, 1, 10), _rand_label_puny(rng), rng.choice(["com", "de", "jp", "cn"])]
    elif mode == 4:
        # numeric-ish labels
        num = str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
        labels = ["host" + num, "svc" + str(rng.randint(0, 999)), rng.choice(["local", "lan", "example"]) ]
    elif mode == 5:
        # hyphenated interior
        def hyphen_label():
            a = _rand_label(rng, 2, 6)
            b = _rand_label(rng, 2, 6)
            return a + "-" + b
        labels = [hyphen_label(), _rand_label(rng, 2, 10), rng.choice(["com", "co", "uk", "io"]).strip('.')]
    elif mode == 6:
        # wildcard dNSName for certs
        base = _rand_label(rng, 3, 12) + "." + rng.choice(["example", _rand_label(rng, 3, 10)]) + "." + rng.choice(["com","net","org"]) 
        return "*." + base
    else:
        # long labels near limit but <= 63 chars per label and total <= 253
        first = _rand_label(rng, 10, 20)
        middle = _rand_label(rng, 20, 30)
        tld = rng.choice(["international", "technology", "solutions", "example"])  # each <= 63
        labels = [first, middle, tld]

    name = ".".join(labels)
    # With small probability, add a trailing dot to make it FQDN form (still valid)
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(name) < 250:
        name += "."
    # With small probability, mix case
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        chars = []
        for ch in name:
            if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.5:
                ch = ch.upper()
            chars.append(ch)
        name = ''.join(chars)
    # Ensure total length <= 253 (without trailing dot); if too long, trim middle label.
    base = name[:-1] if name.endswith('.') else name
    if len(base) > 253:
        parts = base.split('.')
        for i in range(len(parts)):
            if len(base) <= 253:
                break
            if len(parts[i]) > 1:
                parts[i] = parts[i][:max(1, len(parts[i]) - (len(base) - 253))]
                base = '.'.join(parts)
        name = base + ('.' if name.endswith('.') else '')
    return name


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate one primary DNS name.
    dns = _rand_domain(rng)

    # Occasionally return multiple candidates concatenated with a comma to
    # exercise parsers that may split lists in some contexts. However, the
    # provided fuzzer stubs pass a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as a blob for
    # one SAN element, so we mostly return a single DNS. Keep comma-join rare.
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        extra = _rand_domain(rng)
        combined = dns + "," + extra
        return combined.encode('ascii')[:4096]

    return dns.encode('ascii')[:4096]

]

# Helper to build IPv6 bytes from hextets

def ipv6_bytes(hextets: List[int]) -> bytes:
    return b"".join(struct.pack("!H", h & 0xFFFF) for h in hextets[:8])

IPv6_COMMON = [
    ipv6_bytes([0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1]),                 # ::1 loopback
    ipv6_bytes([0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]),                 # :: unspecified
    ipv6_bytes([0xFE80, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1]),            # fe80::1 link-local
    ipv6_bytes([0x2001, 0x4860, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x8888]),  # 2001:4860::8888 (like Google DNS v6)
    ipv6_bytes([0x2001, 0xdb8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1]),        # documentation prefix
]

# 6to4 mapped example: 2002:V4HIGH:V4LOW::

def ipv6_6to4_from_v4(v4: bytes) -> bytes:
    a, b, c, d = v4
    v4word = (a << 8) | b
    v4word2 = (c << 8) | d
    return ipv6_bytes([0x2002, v4word, v4word2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0])

# IPv4-mapped IPv6: ::ffff:a.b.c.d

def ipv6_mapped_from_v4(v4: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00" * 10 + b"\xff\xff" + v4

# Generate a random but valid IPv4 address with weighted special ranges

def gen_ipv4_r(seed_rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = seed_rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        return seed_rng.choice(IPv4_COMMON)
    # Random private or global
    which = seed_rng.randint(0, 4)
    if which == 0:  # 10.0.0.0/8
        return bytes([10, seed_rng.randrange(256), seed_rng.randrange(256), seed_rng.randrange(256)])
    if which == 1:  # 172.16.0.0/12
        return bytes([172, seed_rng.randrange(16, 32), seed_rng.randrange(256), seed_rng.randrange(256)])
    if which == 2:  # 192.168.0.0/16
        return bytes([192, 168, seed_rng.randrange(256), seed_rng.randrange(256)])
    if which == 3:  # 100.64.0.0/10 (CGNAT)
        return bytes([100, seed_rng.randrange(64, 128), seed_rng.randrange(256), seed_rng.randrange(256)])
    # global unicast, avoid multicast 224/4 and 0/8, 127/8
    while True:
        a = seed_rng.randrange(1, 256)
        if a in (127,) or 224 <= a <= 239:
            continue
        b = seed_rng.randrange(256)
        c = seed_rng.randrange(256)
        d = seed_rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes([a, b, c, d])

# Generate a random but valid IPv6 with some interesting patterns

def gen_ipv6_r(seed_rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = seed_rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        # choose from curated set
        return seed_rng.choice(IPv6_COMMON)
    if choice < 0.7:
        # IPv4-mapped or 6to4
        v4 = gen_ipv4_r(seed_rng)
        return seed_rng.choice([ipv6_mapped_from_v4(v4), ipv6_6to4_from_v4(v4)])
    # Random global unicast 2000::/3
    hextets = []
    first = seed_rng.randrange(0x2000, 0x6000)  # 001 to 011 prefix -> 2000::/3
    hextets.append(first)
    for _ in range(7):
        hextets.append(seed_rng.randrange(0, 0x10000))
    return ipv6_bytes(hextets)

# Compose the final buffer the fuzzer will use via FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# The stub may truncate/resize to 4 or 16 bytes. We'll place multiple candidates
# concatenated so truncations still yield valid addresses, and longer uses get valid 16-byte sequences.

def build_buffer(seed_rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Start with a strong IPv6 candidate (16 bytes)
    parts.append(gen_ipv6_r(seed_rng))
    # Follow by an IPv4 (4 bytes) so small truncations still get valid IPv4
    parts.append(gen_ipv4_r(seed_rng))
    # Add mapped and 6to4 forms to exercise encoding branches
    v4 = gen_ipv4_r(seed_rng)
    parts.append(ipv6_mapped_from_v4(v4))
    parts.append(ipv6_6to4_from_v4(v4))
    # Add a few curated constants
    parts.append(IPv6_COMMON[0])  # ::1
    parts.append(IPv4_COMMON[0])  # 127.0.0.1
    # Shuffle parts to vary prefix
    seed_rng.shuffle(parts)
    buf = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure within 4096 bytes
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_buffer(rng)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary binary data
# Used by fuzz stubs to feed network recv/send buffers and PKCS7 verification data/cert DER.
# We generate valid-looking payloads that can exercise different code paths:
# - Mixture of plausible DER-encoded certificate beginnings, PEM snippets, and random app data.
# - Include sizes 1..512 (as stubs clamp to 512) and a variety of lengths.
# - Sometimes include ASCII text simulating HTTP/TLS/ALPN, sometimes binary noise.
# - For pkcs7 verify detached data, any bytes are acceptable; we still try to provide structured-like inputs.
# The function returns a single bytes buffer that the harness will split for FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

OID_RSA_SHA256 = b"\x2a\x86\x48\x86\xf7\x0d\x01\x01\x0b"  # 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11
OID_RSA_ENCRYPTION = b"\x2a\x86\x48\x86\xf7\x0d\x01\x01\x01"  # 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1


def _rand_ipv4(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return ".".join(str(rnd.randint(1, 254)) for _ in range(4))


def _rand_hostname(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    labels = [
        ''.join(rnd.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789') for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 10)))
        for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 4))
    ]
    return ".".join(labels)


def _tls_client_hello_like(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce a TLS-like ClientHello record header + random payload
    # TLS record header: type(0x16), version(0x0303), length(2 bytes)
    payload_len = rnd.randint(32, 256)
    hdr = bytes([0x16, 0x03, rnd.choice([0x01, 0x03, 0x04])]) + struct.pack('>H', payload_len)
    # Handshake header: type ClientHello(1), length(3 bytes)
    hs_len = payload_len - 4 if payload_len >= 4 else payload_len
    hs = bytes([0x01]) + struct.pack('>I', hs_len)[1:]
    body = rnd.randbytes(max(0, payload_len - len(hs))) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes([rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(max(0, payload_len - len(hs)))])
    return hdr + hs + body


def _pem_block(rnd: random.Random, typ: str) -> bytes:
    # Simple PEM-like block with base64-ish content
    header = f"-----BEGIN {typ}-----\n".encode()
    footer = f"-----END {typ}-----\n".encode()
    b64chars = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
    lines = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(5, 20)):
        line = bytes(rnd.choice(b64chars) for _ in range(rnd.randint(48, 64)))
        lines.append(line + b"\n")
    return header + b"".join(lines) + footer


def _der_like_cert(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal DER SEQUENCE with some OIDs to look like parts of a cert
    def der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
        if n < 0x80:
            return bytes([n])
        s = n.to_bytes((n.bit_length() + 7)//8, 'big')
        return bytes([0x80 | len(s)]) + s

    # Build AlgorithmIdentifier: SEQ { OID sha256WithRSAEncryption, NULL }
    alg_seq = b"\x06" + der_len(len(OID_RSA_SHA256)) + OID_RSA_SHA256 + b"\x05\x00"
    alg = b"\x30" + der_len(len(alg_seq)) + alg_seq

    # SubjectPublicKeyInfo: SEQ { alg rsaEncryption NULL, BIT STRING random }
    spk_alg_seq = b"\x06" + der_len(len(OID_RSA_ENCRYPTION)) + OID_RSA_ENCRYPTION + b"\x05\x00"
    spk_alg = b"\x30" + der_len(len(spk_alg_seq)) + spk_alg_seq
    bit_payload_len = rnd.randint(64, 256)
    bit_payload = (b"\x00" + (rnd.randbytes(bit_payload_len) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes([rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(bit_payload_len)])))
    spk = spk_alg + b"\x03" + der_len(len(bit_payload)) + bit_payload
    spki = b"\x30" + der_len(len(spk)) + spk

    # TBSCertificate (very rough, just some fields): SEQ { version [0] EXPLICIT INTEGER 2, serial INTEGER, alg, issuer SEQ, validity SEQ, subject SEQ, spki }
    version = b"\xa0\x03\x02\x01\x02"
    serial = b"\x02\x01" + bytes([rnd.randint(1, 200)])
    name = b"\x30\x00"  # empty name
    # validity: SEQ of two UTCTime (fake minimal strings)
    not_before = b"\x17\x0d" + b"240101000000Z"
    not_after = b"\x17\x0d" + b"260101000000Z"
    validity = b"\x30" + der_len(len(not_before)+len(not_after)) + not_before + not_after

    tbs_body = version + serial + alg + name + validity + name + spki
    tbs = b"\x30" + der_len(len(tbs_body)) + tbs_body

    # Certificate: SEQ { tbs, alg, signature BIT STRING }
    sig = (b"\x00" + (rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(64, 128)) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes([rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(rnd.randint(64, 128))])))
    cert_body = tbs + alg + b"\x03" + der_len(len(sig)) + sig
    cert = b"\x30" + der_len(len(cert_body)) + cert_body
    return cert


def _http_like(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    host = _rand_hostname(rnd)
    return (f"GET /{host} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {host}\r\nUser-Agent: fuzz/1.0\r\nAccept: */*\r\n\r\n".encode())


def _mix_chunks(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Include a DER-like cert sometimes (useful for pkcs7 cert parsing attempts in fuzz stub)
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        chunks.append(_der_like_cert(rnd))
    # Include PEM-like blocks sometimes
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(_pem_block(rnd, rnd.choice(["CERTIFICATE", "PKCS7", "PUBLIC KEY"])) )
    # TLS-like record
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(_tls_client_hello_like(rnd))
    # Some HTTP-like data
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(_http_like(rnd))
    # Random binary application data sized <= 512
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        ln = rnd.randint(1, 512)
        data = rnd.randbytes(ln) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes([rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(ln)])
        chunks.append(data)
    # Include IPv4/IPv6 textual and URI
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(_rand_ipv4(rnd).encode())
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        chunks.append(f"https://{_rand_hostname(rnd)}/path".encode())
    return chunks


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = _mix_chunks(rnd)

    # Shuffle to vary ordering
    rnd.shuffle(parts)

    # Concatenate with small delimiters occasionally
    out = bytearray()
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        # Clamp any very large part; the stubs cap to 512 anyway, but keep overall under MAX_TOTAL
        if len(p) > 1024:
            p = p[:1024]
        out += p
        if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
            out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
            break
        if i != len(parts) - 1 and rnd.random() < 0.4:
            out += b"\r\n"
        if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
            out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
            break

    # Ensure non-empty and not exceeding limit
    if not out:
        out.extend(b"a")
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        del out[MAX_TOTAL:]

    return bytes(out)
